newsitem.title: USA: Morrison Knudsen sees Sept. 11 merger.
newsitem.headline: Morrison Knudsen sees Sept. 11 merger.

text.p: Morrison Knudsen Corp said Monday it expects its merger with Washington Construction Group to be effective Sept. 11, now that the plan has been approved by a bankruptcy judge.
Under the merger Montana construction mogul Dennis Washington will be chairman of the new merged company, which will be known as Morrison Knudsen Corp and headquartered in Boise.
Robert Tinstman, who was named as president and chief executive officer of the troubled company last year, will continue in those capacities for the new company.
"Dennis Washington's decision to serve as chairman of the company underscores his commitment to MK and our clients," Tinstman said in a statement.
Dorn Parkinson, chairman of Dennis Washington's Washington Corp and Washington Construction Group Inc, will be a vice chairman of the new Morrison Knudsen.
Robert Miller, currently chairman of Morrison Knudsen, will be the other vice chairman.
Miller, best known for helping to engineer Chrysler Corp's turnaround in the 1980s, was brought in last year after the board ousted former chairman William Agee.

It was under the free-spending Agee that Morrison Knudsen -- whose storied 84-year history includes such marquee projects as the Hoover Dam and San Francisco Bay Bridge -- ran up the losses that drove it into bankruptcy court.

Over two years, the company's losses have totaled more than $600 million, and it filed the prepackaged bankruptcy plan in June after Washington agreed to buy it for about $265 million in cash, stock and debt assumption.
Morrison Knudsen said that after the merger it will be essentially debt free with a net worth of $300 million, revenues approaching $2 billion and a backlog of $4 billion.

The company, with some 10,000 employees, said it had obtained a $200 million credit facility for the next five years with the Bank of Montreal as agent. The company said it also has reached a bonding arrangement.

Tinstman said in an interview that he expected the new Morrison to be profitable immediately once the merger is effective. He said all of Morrison Knudsen's clients stayed with the company during the reorganization period.

Management will be essentially unchanged from the current Morrison Knudsen with the exception that Darrol Groven, a Washington Construction executive, will be in charge of the heavy civil construction group.
Other directors will be Terry Payne, Leonard Judd, David Batchelder, John Roach and William Langley.
After the name change the current Washington Construction Group will trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "MK."
